qualification.details: A graduate degree in Medicine (M.B.B.S.) or equivalent from a recognized university/institution included in the first schedule to the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956. Enrolled in any State Medical Register maintained under the Act. Completed compulsory rotating internship. Post Graduate Degree or Diploma in the related specialty mentioned in Section 'A' or Section 'B' in Schedule I to the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956 (102 of 1956), or equivalent. Doctorate of Medicine (DM) or Magister Chirurgiae (M.Ch.) or equivalent, with three years' experience in the concerned Super-Specialty after obtaining the first postgraduate degree (Senior Residency period will also be counted towards experience). Must have permanent registration from MCI/NMC/State Medical Council before appointment. | A recognized medical qualification of Allopathic system of medicine included in the first or second schedule or Part-II of the third schedule (other than licentiate qualification) to the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956. Holders of qualifications in Part-II of the third schedule must also fulfil the conditions in Sub-Section (3) of Section 13 of the Act. Permanent registration from MCI/NMC/State Medical Council is required before appointment in any CAPF/AR. Completion of compulsory rotating internship. Post Graduate (PG) Degree/Diploma in the concerned specialty mentioned in Section 'A' or Section 'B' in Schedule-I, or equivalent, along with one and a half years' experience in the concerned speciality after obtaining the PG Degree, or two and a half years' experience after obtaining the PG Diploma. | A recognized medical qualification of allopathic system of medicine included in the first or second schedule or Part-II of the third schedule (other than licentiate qualification) to the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956; Part-II third schedule holders must also fulfil the conditions in Sub-Section (3) of Section 13. Permanent registration from any MCI/NMC/State Medical Council before appointment in any CAPF/AR. Completion of compulsory rotating internship. Candidates undergoing rotating internship are eligible to apply and appear for the interview, provided that, if selected, they satisfactorily complete the compulsory internship before appointment.

Candidates whose online applications are found in order will be issued an e-admit card mentioning date
time and venue for Documentation & Interview by a designated Board of Officers
followed by Physical Standard Tests (PST) and Medical Examination Tests (MET)
to assess suitability for appointment in CAPFs & AR.
All candidates called for interview must bring a clear
legible printout of the e-admit card along with original testimonials and one set of self-attested copies

including: Matriculation/School Leaving Certificate (age proof); certificate in support of qualification; certificate for completion/undergoing internship; registration certificate from MCI/NMC/State Medical Council; SC/ST/OBC/EWS certificates (as applicable

issued by an authority not below Tehsildar/SDO or equivalent); OBC (NCL) declaration; NOC for Government Servants; discharge certificate for Ex-Servicemen; domicile/citizenship proof; West Pakistani Refugee certificate (if applicable); height relaxation certificate (if applicable); and NCC Grade Certificates
where available. Candidates without these original documents may not be permitted to enter the interview centre.
The designated board conducts the interview of candidates found eligible after documentation. The interview carries 200 marks and tests general knowledge and ability in the candidate's academic field
along with personality
intellectual curiosity
judgment
alertness
social cohesion
integrity of character
initiative and leadership capability. The minimum qualifying standard is 40% of the total marks (i.e.
80 out of 200)
and this minimum is the same for all categories of candidates. Candidates not meeting this standard are eliminated from the selection process.

Candidates who qualify the interview are checked for physical standards by a designated Board of Officers on the same day or the next day. Candidates who do not meet the minimum required physical standards are eliminated at this stage
though they may prefer an appeal the same day to the nominated appellate authority through the Presiding Officer of the PST Board; the appellate authority's decision is final.
Height is relaxable by 2 cms for candidates falling in the categories of Gorkhas
Garhwalis
Kumaonis
Dogras
Marathas
and candidates belonging to the States of Sikkim
Nagaland
Arunachal Pradesh
Manipur
Tripura
Mizoram
Meghalaya
Assam
Himachal Pradesh
the Kashmir region of UT Jammu & Kashmir

and UT of Ladakh; and relaxable by 3 cms for candidates belonging to Scheduled Tribes. Candidates seeking such relaxation must submit the prescribed certificate whenever sought by the Recruitment Board.
Candidates who qualify the PST undergo Medical Examination Test by a duly constituted Board of Medical Officers of CAPFs & AR
on the same day or the following day of the PST
as per medical guidelines issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA UO No. A.VI-1/2014-Rectt (SSB) dated 20/05/2015

as amended). Candidates are declared either "FIT" or "UNFIT". Those declared unfit may undergo a "Review Medical Examination (RME)" by giving written consent within 24 hours of being informed of their unfitness; RME is conducted preferably the next day.
No Radial Keratotomy (RK) or other refraction surgery is permitted. Lasik surgery correction is permitted subject to prescribed criteria: interval of 6 months since surgery
age 20–35 years
axial length less than 26 mm and more than 21 mm
corneal thickness of 425 microns
pre-Lasik error up to 6D
vision as per medical guidelines
and normal retinal status.
Candidates must not have knock-knees
flat foot or squint
and must be in good mental and bodily health
free from any medical condition or physical defect likely to interfere with efficient performance of duties.
Tattoo clause: Tattoos depicting religious symbols/figures and the name (as followed in the Indian Army) are permitted. Tattoos are allowed only on the inner aspect of the forearm - left forearm only
being the non-saluting limb - or on the dorsum of the hands
and the size must be less than one-fourth of the particular body part (elbow or hand). Where a tattoo has been removed and has substantially faded
it will be treated as a "scar" and not a tattoo
subject to review by the Medical Board during detailed medical examination.
The Medical Officers Selection Board will prepare a merit list based on the aggregate marks awarded to each candidate during the interview. Separate merit lists are also compiled for SC/ST
OBC (NCL) and EWS candidates.
how_to_apply: Eligible and interested candidates have to apply online through the ITBP Recruitment website: www.recruitment.itbpolice.nic.in. No other mode of application submission is allowed.
Visit the official ITBP Recruitment website: www.recruitment.itbpolice.nic.in
Refer to the FAQs and "How to Register" links on the website before starting.
Fill your profile and apply online strictly as per the eligibility criteria and instructions given, to avoid disqualification at a later stage.

Upload a clear and legible photo, scanned signature, certificate in support of MBBS or equivalent qualification, certificate for specialized qualification issued by the recognized university, and registration certificate of MCI/NMC/State Medical Council.
Provide a genuine and functional e-mail ID and mobile number, since admit card and all further communication will be sent to these details.
Pay the applicable application fee (if not exempted) through the online payment gateway before the closing date.
Regularly check your registered e-mail (including the spam/junk folder) and the ITBP Recruitment website for updates on admit card and further notices.

Note: ITBP will not be responsible for failure to receive the admit card online, or for power failure, electronic or internet-related problems faced by candidates while applying online. Candidates should come prepared for more than one day's stay under their own arrangements at the recruitment centre, as ITBP reserves the right to issue online admit cards at short notice.

content_sections.heading: ITBP CAPF MOSB Medical Officer Salary
content_sections.text: In addition to basic pay, officers are entitled to Non-Practicing Allowance, Dearness Allowance, Transport Allowance, House Rent Allowance and other allowances admissible under Central Government orders/provisions, as amended from time to time. No Post Graduate allowance is admissible, since a Post Graduate degree/diploma (or graduate degree/diploma in a particular field of specialization, as applicable) is the basic essential qualification for the post. A Dynamic Assured Career Progression (DACP) Scheme grants time-scale financial upgradation to Medical Officers in CAPFs & AR without linkage to vacancy, based on years of regular service in each pay level. Broadly: Medical Officers (Assistant Commandant): progress through Level-10 → Level-11 (4 years) → Level-12 (5 years) → Level-13 (4 years) → Level-13-A (3 years) → Level-14 (4 years, along with 20 years of regular service), with corresponding ranks from Deputy Commandant up to Commandant. Specialist Medical Officers (Deputy Commandant): progress through Level-11 → Level-12 (2 years) → Level-13 (4 years) → Level-13-A (3 years) → Level-14 (4 years), with corresponding ranks from Second-in-Command up to Commandant. Super Specialist Medical Officers (Second-in-Command): progress through Level-12 → Level-13 (4 years) → Level-13-A (3 years) → Level-14 (4 years), with corresponding ranks up to Commandant. Promotion from the rank of Commandant to DIG (Medical) and IG (Medical) for Medical Officers and Specialist Medical Officers is by selection against sanctioned vacancy through a combined seniority list. An officer can apply for the PG entrance examination on completion of 5 years of regular service, as per the instructions issued in this regard.

faq.question: Q1. What is CAPF MOSB Medical Officer Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: It is a recruitment drive conducted by the CAPF Medical Officer Selection Board-2025 (MOSB-2025), through the ITBP, Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, to fill 282 Group 'A' posts of Super Specialist Medical Officer (Second-in-Command), Specialist Medical Officer (Deputy Commandant) and Medical Officer (Assistant Commandant) in BSF, CRPF, ITBP, SSB and Assam Rifles.

faq.question: Q2. How many vacancies are available in CAPF MOSB Medical Officer Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: A total of 282 vacancies: 05 Super Specialist Medical Officer, 162 Specialist Medical Officer, and 115 Medical Officer posts (including a 10% reservation for Ex-Servicemen within the Medical Officer posts).

faq.question: Q3. What is the last date to apply for CAPF MOSB Medical Officer Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The online application window opens on 10-08-2026 at 00:01 AM and closes on 08-09-2026 at 11:59 PM.

faq.question: Q4. What is the qualification required for CAPF MOSB Medical Officer posts?
faq.answer: A recognized MBBS or equivalent medical qualification registered with MCI/NMC/State Medical Council, with completion of compulsory rotating internship. Specialist and Super Specialist posts additionally require postgraduate/super-specialty qualifications and specified years of experience, as detailed in the eligibility section above.

faq.question: Q5. What is the age limit for CAPF MOSB Medical Officer Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Maximum 50 years for Super Specialist Medical Officer, 40 years for Specialist Medical Officer, and 30 years for Medical Officer, as on the closing date of application, with age relaxation available for SC/ST, OBC(NCL), Government servants and other specified categories.

faq.question: Q6. What is the application fee for CAPF MOSB Medical Officer Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: ₹400 for male candidates belonging to General (UR), OBC and EWS categories. SC, ST, Ex-Servicemen and all Female candidates are exempted from the application fee.

faq.question: Q7. How can I apply online for CAPF MOSB Medical Officer Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Applications must be submitted online only, through www.recruitment.itbpolice.nic.in, along with the required photo, signature, qualification and registration certificates, before the closing date.

faq.answer: Selection is through Documentation, followed by an Interview (200 marks, minimum qualifying 40%/80 marks), Physical Standard Test (PST), and Medical Examination Test (MET), with a final merit list prepared on the basis of interview marks.
